title: Personal Loans Servicing Standard: Charging the Returned-Payment Fee and the Returned-Payment Fee Tool
content:
## Rule

When a posted payment on a Personal Loans loan comes back unpaid with a return code that bears a fee (R01, R02, R03, R04, R08, R09, R16 or R20), one returned-payment fee is charged against that return, at most one per returned payment and no more than the grade's monthly maximum of returned-payment fees on a loan in one calendar month. The fee of the latest returned payment on the loan (on a tie of dates, the first one recorded), when its return code bears a fee, is worked out under the Personal Loans returned-payment fee figuring; a fee owed on any earlier fee-bearing return is charged at the schedule amount, unreduced, because that figuring weighs the bounce being handled now, and a fee for an earlier bounce that was not charged when it happened is a catch-up charge at the schedule amount.

A returned-payment fee that works out to 0.00, as it always does on schedule C, is not charged: no fee line is written, and it does not count toward the returned-payment fees charged on the loan in that calendar month.

| Returned payment | Fee amount |
|---|---|
| the latest returned payment on the loan, fee-bearing code | worked out under the returned-payment fee figuring |
| an earlier fee-bearing returned payment | the schedule amount, unreduced |
| code R07, R10, R29 or a debit card chargeback | no fee |

## The returned-payment fee tool

**What it does.** `assess_returned_payment_fee_e467aa52` records one returned-payment fee line on a Personal Loans loan, dated today, pointing at the returned-payment line it is charged for, under the named state fee schedule, and adds the fee to the loan's unpaid fees. Nothing else on the loan changes. Once recorded, the fee appears in the loan's ledger and the loan's unpaid fees are higher by the fee amount.

**How it is invoked.** It is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `assess_returned_payment_fee_e467aa52` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning and format |
|---|---|
| `loan_id` | reference number of the personal loan charged, as returned by the loan lookup |
| `customer_id` | reference number of the borrower who owns that loan, as returned by the customer profile lookup |
| `related_txn_id` | reference number of the returned-payment ledger line the fee is charged for, as returned by the loan ledger lookup |
| `fee_schedule` | state fee schedule the fee is charged under, exactly one of `schedule_a` (fee schedule A), `schedule_b` (fee schedule B), `schedule_c` (fee schedule C) |
| `amount` | the returned-payment fee in USD, a decimal number with 2 decimal places; stored rounded to the cent |

**Return.** A one-line confirmation of the form "Returned-payment fee <ledger line id> charged on loan <loan id> for return <returned line id>: <USD with 2 decimals> under <schedule>; unpaid fees now <USD with 2 decimals>." The ledger line id is the reference number of the new fee; its presence means the fee was recorded.
